content.title: Five celebs BANNED from Oscars for life – ‘Repugnant’ producer and disgraced Godfather actor on the list
content.text: THE Academy doesn’t mess around regarding who can attend its coveted awards ceremony, as multiple celebrities have been banned from Hollywood’s biggest night for violating its code of conduct. Ahead of the 98th annual Oscar Awards on Sunday, March 15, we’re reminded that numerous once-celebrated A-listers have been axed from the guest list, and the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is standing firm on never welcoming them back. Sign up for the Entertainment newsletter Thank you! Will Smith was banned for 10 years from the Oscars after slapping presenter Chris Rock during the live broadcastCredit: Getty Below are five famous stars who have been prohibited from stepping through the doors of the prestigious event forever. Carmine Caridi The Godfather Part II star Carmine Caridi received a lifetime ban by the Academy after being caught pirating screenersCredit: Getty – Contributor Fans of 1974’s The Godfather Part II will recall Carmine Caridi, who portrayed mobster Carmine Rosato in the iconic sequel film. He also appeared in The Godfather Part III, released in 1990, as a different character, Albert Volpe, and as Detective Vince Gotelli in NYPD: Blue. Carmine died in 2019 at 85, but he’d been blacklisted from the Oscars long before, becoming the first-ever member of the Academy to be expelled. The actor was caught pirating screeners designated only for members to view for voting purposes and allowing their circulation on the internet, resulting in his ban from the organization in 2004. Harvey Weinstein Harvey Weinstein was banned forever from the awards show after produce’s sexual assault accusations came to lightCredit: AP:Associated Press It shouldn’t come as a shock to viewers that producer and convicted sex offender Harvey Weinstein, who is currently serving a 16-year prison sentence for sexual assault and rape, has a lifetime ban from the awards show. He was expelled in 2017, shortly after the New York Times reported sexual assault accusations against him from multiple women spanning over three decades. The Academy branded the disgraced film producer’s actions as “repugnant, abhorrent, and antithetical to the high standards of the academy and the creative community it represents.” Most read in Entertainment Harvey wasn’t stripped of his Oscar Award for Best Picture for his 1998 film, Shakespeare in Love, but his actions prompted the Academy to put a new code of conduct in place, stating that the organization doesn’t tolerate “people who abuse their status, power or influence in a manner that violates standards of decency.” Bill Cosby The Academy forbid actor Bill Cosby from attending future ceremonies after his 2018 conviction of drugging and assaulting Andrea ConstandCredit: EPA Bill Cosby went from being a household name and celebrated actor to another fallen star on the Academy’s list of banned celebs. The comedian was expelled from the organization a month after his 2018 conviction of drugging and assaulting basketball player Andrea Constand. He was released from prison in 2021 after his sexual assault conviction was overturned on a technicality by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. Roman Polanski Filmmaker Roman Polanski was booted from the Academy in 1977 after pleading guilty to unlawful sex with a minorCredit: AFP – Getty At the same time as The Cosby Show alum‘s expulsion, Roman Polanski was also booted from the Academy. The filmmaker retreated to France in 1977 after pleading guilty to unlawful sex with a 13-year-old girl, and he hasn’t returned to the awards show since. Most Awarded Oscar Winners of All Time Best Director: John Ford — 4 wins The Informer (1935) The Grapes of Wrath (1940) How Green Was My Valley (1941) The Quiet Man (1952) Frank Capra — 3 wins It Happened One Night (1934) Mr. Deeds Goes to Town (1936) You Can’t Take It with You (1938) William Wyler — 3 wins Mrs. Miniver (1942) The Best Years of Our Lives (1946) Ben-Hur (1959) Best Actor in a Leading Role: Daniel Day‑Lewis — 3 wins (most in history) My Left Foot (1989) There Will Be Blood (2007) Lincoln (2012) A slew of actors are tied in second place having won 2 Oscars, including: Marlon Brando, Tom Hanks, Dustin Hoffman, Sean Penn, Anthony Hopkins, and more. Best Actress in a Leading Role: Katharine Hepburn — 4 wins Morning Glory (1933) Guess Who’s Coming to Dinner (1967) The Lion in Winter (1968) On Golden Pond (1981) Frances McDormand — 3 wins Fargo (1996) Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2017) Nomadland (2020) Meryl Streep — 3 wins (two lead, one supporting) Kramer vs. Kramer (1979) — Supporting Actress Sophie’s Choice (1982) — Lead Actress The Iron Lady (2011) — Lead Actress Best Actor in a Supporting Role: Walter Brennan — 3 wins Come and Get It (1936) Kentucky (1938) The Westerner (1940) Many actors are tied for the second place honor with 2 nominations, including: Michael Caine, Denzel Washington, Gene Hackman, Jack Nicholson, Christoph Waltz, and Mahershala Ali. Best Actress in a Supporting Role: Dianne Wiest — 2 wins Hannah and Her Sisters (1986) Bullets Over Broadway (1994) Shelley Winters — 2 wins The Diary of Anne Frank (1959) A Patch of Blue (1965) Maggie Smith — 2 wins The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie (1969) — Lead Actress California Suite (1978) — Supporting Actress However, he has still received numerous Oscar nominations and even nabbed the Best Director award for The Pianist in 2003, given that his eligibility to win awards remains. Adam Kimmel Cinematographer Adam Kimmel was expelled from the Academy after his past as a sex offender came to lightCredit: Getty In 2021, cinematographer Adam Kimmel was expelled from the Academy when it came to light that he was a sex offender. In the film world, Adam was best known for Jesus’ Son (1999), Capote (2005), and Lars and the Real Girl (2007); however, he was immediately wiped from the Academy’s guest list when the organization learned of his two arrests for statutory assaults on minors. Like the others, Adam was found to be in violation of the Academy’s code of conduct and was expelled. Temporary Bans Will accepted the Oscar for Best Actor shortly after his altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 ceremonyCredit: EPA While these celebrities received lifetime bans, the Academy was more lenient toward others who violated its rules. Richard Gere was banned from the Oscars after he went off script while presenting the award for Best Art Direction during the 1993 ceremony. Instead of reading the teleprompter like he was told, the Pretty Woman actor made some shocking remarks about the conflict between Tibet and China. He was supposedly prohibited from attending the show for 20 years, although the Academy reportedly told GQ, “We don’t ban presenters.” Most recently, Will Smith was smacked with a 10-year ban from the ceremony for slapping presenter Chris Rock onstage at the 2022 awards show. The Bad Boys star accosted Chris after the comedian made an ill-received joke about his wife Jada Pinkett Smith‘s (who has alopecia) shaved head. He then went back to his seat and yelled, “Keep my wife’s name out your f**king mouth!” during the live broadcast. Will returned to the stage later in the night to accept the award for Best Actor for his role as Richard Williams in King Richard and received a standing ovation from the audience. Months later, Will released a YouTube video apologizing to Chris, and the comic went on to mock the altercation in his stand-up specials. Harvey is currently serving a 16-year prison sentence for sexual assault and rapeCredit: EPA Comments
